cleared.check: Task 1, method and proof of execution. The harness of cycle 16 (category-labs/monad v0.16.7 with asmjit e8c8e2e4 and evmc f6b7c57e, v0.16.5 with evmc 34795f4e, the release keccak) was relinked with two recompiled objects only: a copy of category/vm/compiler/ir/x86.cpp that, at chosen EVM pcs, emits an execution counter before the instruction (rax saved to and restored from a fixed address, mov and lea only, so flags and the virtual stack are untouched) and optionally, after the instruction, a call that records the word the instruction left on top of the stack (the code of Emitter::runtime_print_top1); and interpreter/execute.cpp built with a copy of instruction_table.hpp whose MONAD_VM_NEXT and MONAD_VM_NEXT_PUSH record the stack top at the same pcs. emitter.cpp is not changed. Two ways of reaching the sites were used: PoolManager calls (pc 12232, 15519, 22378, 22639) and, for operands no call can supply and for pc 16642, an entry into the deployed runtime's own basic block: bytes 0..46 of the 24,009-byte runtime are replaced by a 45-byte prologue (copy calldata[0x120:] to memory 0, push eight calldata words, jump to calldata word 0; a JUMPDEST at pc 38 stores the top word and returns it), the other 23,962 bytes unchanged. Entries used: 0x5703 (the 2^128 copy of mulDiv, called from Position.update at pcs 5969 and 5981), 0x5810 (the 2^96 copy, called from getAmount1Delta at pcs 23088 and 23161), 0x3c94 (Hooks.beforeSwap after the hook call) and 0x40d7 (the bytes4 mask block).
cleared.result: Arm identity. In the v0.16.7 asm log (which prints a comment per EVM instruction) the text emitted for each of the five site instructions is identical between the plain build, the counter build (once the five counter lines are removed; the rest of the 48,691-line log is identical) and the single-site capture builds (the plain text is a prefix of the capture build's text). The texts are: pc 22378 MULMOD loads a from [rbp-128..-104] into r13,r14,r15,r12 and b0,b1 from [rbp-96],[rbp-88], computes r10 = lo(a0*b0) by mulx, r11 = hi(a0*b0) + a1*b0 + a0*b1 (64-bit imul) and zeroes r8, r9; pc 22639 is the same with 32-bit imul and add on limb 1 (mod 2^96); pc 15519 SAR(128) of the word in r12..r15 is mov rax,r15; sar rax,63; mov r10,r14; mov r11,r15; mov r8,rax; mov r9,rax; pc 16642 SHL(3) of the word in r12..r15 is three shld and one shl by 3; pc 12232 CALLDATALOAD is the bswap_to_ymm arm with the bound test on the offset limbs and the 32-byte vmovups read. In v0.16.5 the same instructions open each site's text (v0.16.5 prints no per-instruction comment, so the text was located by the counter lines). Compiled from the prologue runtime, the enclosing blocks B5703, B5810, B3c94 and B40d7 equal the deployed runtime's blocks once label numbers, block numbers and read-only data offsets are replaced by the bytes they point to (both compiled in one process so that host pointers agree); the one exception, B3c94 under v0.16.5, differs only in the order of three independent stores at the block exit (see the v0.16.5 heap-address item). Marker counts, native = interpreter in every file and on both releases: pc 22378 274 (prologue) + 18 (ordinary calls); pc 22639 200 (prologue) + 57 (ordinary swaps) + 188 (hook swaps); pc 15519 116 (prologue) + 648 (ordinary swaps through a returns-delta hook); pc 16642 47 (prologue only); pc 12232 1,220 (ordinary extsload and exttload calls). Every file gives 0 mismatches between interpreter and native in status, gas, return data, storage, transient storage, balances, logs and the captured site words.

cleared.result: v0.16.7 and v0.16.5: native MULMOD word = interpreter word = Python (a * b) mod 2^128 for all 274 executions; 118 of them with prod1 = 1 and 2 with prod1 at the largest allowed value. The function's return value equals Python floor(a * b / 2^128) in all 283 calls that return, and the 73 calls with prod1 >= 2^128 revert, as the require at FullMath.sol:30 says. prod0 = 2^96 - 1 with prod1 = 1 was not built: no factor of 2^256 + 2^96 - 1 was found by trial division and a short Pollard search.

cleared.check: Task 2 from the source: which callers pass a constant denominator, which pc each compiles to, and whether a wrong remainder at prod1 = 1 could become an accepted amount.
cleared.result: Callers. Position.update passes FixedPoint128.Q128 (src/libraries/Position.sol:93-96); both calls jump to 0x5703 (pcs 5969 and 5981), whose MULMOD is pc 22378. SqrtPriceMath.getAmount1Delta passes denominator = FixedPoint96.Q96 (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:240, :250); both of its compiled copies jump to 0x5810 (pcs 23088 and 23161), whose MULMOD is pc 22639. SqrtPriceMath.sol:97 and :105 pass Q96 as the multiplier with liquidity as the denominator (copy at 0x588a and mulDivRoundingUp, MULMOD by a runtime call), and SwapMath.sol:65, :74 and :104 use the denominator 1e6 (copy with MULMOD at pc 22513, runtime call); these are not mul_mod2 sites. Arithmetic. For a power-of-two denominator N = 2^k the correct remainder is prod0 mod N, which is never above prod0, so gt(remainder, prod0) at FullMath.sol:52 is 0 on a correct node and prod1 stays 1. The emitted arm can only produce a value below N (limbs 2 and 3 are zeroed, limb 1 is 32-bit for 2^96). With any remainder r below N, FullMath.sol:52-75 return at least 2^(256-k) - 1: 200,000 random cases per site of a Python transcription give a least value of exactly 2^160 - 1 for k = 96 and 2^128 - 1 for k = 128 (the borrow case r > prod0 with prod0 < N). Such a result cannot be accepted: Position.update returns it as feesOwed and Pool.modifyLiquidity casts it with toInt128 (src/libraries/Pool.sol:192, src/libraries/SafeCast.sol:56-58), which reverts at 2^127 and above; getAmount1Delta returns at least 2^160 - 1, and every use reverts in a cast (Pool.sol:222-223 and :232-234 through SqrtPriceMath.sol:278-287 in modifyLiquidity; in a swap, SwapMath.sol:68-69 and :89-91 either cap the step at the target, after which the amount of at least 2^160 - 1 reaches the toInt128 casts at Pool.sol:455 or :459, or the comparison fails and the faulty value is replaced by amountRemaining). A quotient below 2^127 needs a remainder above 2^256 - 2^223 + prod0 at the 2^96 site and above 2^255 + prod0 at the 2^128 site, more than 2^222 above anything the arm can write. So the borrow of L-800 cannot be produced by this arm, and a remainder that stays below N changes an accepted amount on no path.

cleared.check: Task 2, which ordinary call reaches the 2^96 site with prod1 = 1 and from which pool state. 80 scenarios on Monad's two engines: a pool of two ordinary tokens with tick spacing 32767, one position [lo, 27 * 32767] with lo in {5, 8, 10, 13} * 32767, liquidity L between 2^96 and the per-tick maximum (about 2^122.2), the start price just below the lower tick, and a oneForZero swap whose price limit sa + diff is chosen so that 2^256 <= L * diff < 2^257.
cleared.result: Reached with prod1 = 1 in 57 of 80 scenarios (one execution each, native = interpreter = Python on both releases): an exact-input swap of any size below 2^160 (19 of 20 reach it; all 20 swaps succeed, because amountIn = getAmount1Delta(sa, limit, L, true) is at least 2^160 and loses the comparison at SwapMath.sol:69, so the step ends inside the range through getNextSqrtPriceFromInput); an exact-input amount above 2^160 (20 of 20; the step takes the target and the swap reverts with SafeCastOverflow 0x93dafdf1); an exact output of the range's token0 (18 of 20; the step takes the target, amountIn from SwapMath.sol:102 is at least 2^160 and the swap reverts with SafeCastOverflow). Small exact outputs do not reach it (the step's own price distance gives prod1 = 0). The liquidity needed costs little: L = 2^99 over [13 * 32767, 26 * 32767] needs about 2^68 units of token0. modifyLiquidity with the price above the range reaches the same copy through Pool.sol:232-234 and reverts in toInt128 (read; the generated scenarios kept the price below the range). donate does not reach either copy.

cleared.check: Task 2, which ordinary call reaches the 2^128 site with prod1 >= 1. 30 scenarios: a full-range position of liquidity 1 to 2^40, one to four donations of up to 2^127 - 1 in one unlock, then a poke (liquidityDelta 0) and a removal.
cleared.result: 7 scenarios reach pc 22378 (18 executions, all prod1 = 1; native = interpreter = Python on both releases), and every call that reaches it reverts with SafeCastOverflow at Pool.sol:192. prod1 >= 1 here means fees owed to one position of at least 2^128 units of one currency, so on a correct node the site only runs in a call that reverts. Fee growth is credited by donations that the donor pays within the same unlock, so building that state needs 2^128 units of a currency, which only a token the attacker issues provides; the position concerned then holds that token. Fee growth inside a range with initialized ticks does not decrease, so no wrapped difference reaches the site.

cleared.check: pc 16642 (SHL by 3 in block 0x40d7): what it computes and whether any call reaches it.
cleared.result: It is the mask of the Solidity conversion bytes4(data) for data shorter than 4 bytes, computing shl(3, 4 - length), in the HookCallFailed wrapper of Hooks.callHook (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:137). data is the abi.encodeCall calldata sent to the hook, at least 36 bytes long, so the branch at pc 16370 never jumps there (as cycle 15 read). No call can execute it. Through the prologue it ran 47 times with lengths 0 to 5, 31 to 33, 2^64, around 2^253, 2^255, 2^256 - 4 to 2^256 - 1 and 30 random words: native = interpreter = Python on both releases.

cleared.check: pc 12232 (CALLDATALOAD of the array length in the decoder of extsload(bytes32[]) and exttload(bytes32[]), selectors 0xdbd035ff and 0x9bf6645f, src/Extsload.sol:42 and src/Exttload.sol:18). 1,348 direct calls: offset words 0x20 to 0x3ffff including unaligned ones, lengths 0 to 64, 2^32, 2^64 - 1, 2^64, 2^255 and 2^256 - 1, calldata tails of 0, 1 and 31 bytes, and the length word ending exactly at the end of calldata and one byte short of it.
cleared.result: 1,220 calls reach pc 12232 (the others fail the decoder's offset or bound checks first); native = interpreter at the site and in the whole run on both releases. The decoder reverts unless offset + 0x23 < calldatasize, so the load at this pc always reads 32 bytes inside calldata; the arm's short-read and out-of-range paths cannot run here.

cleared.check: Task 4. A fault planted in the native code after each site's instruction, one at a time (HX_FAULT_PC): bit 127 of the remainder cleared at pc 22378, bit 95 at pc 22639, no sign fill in the top word at pc 15519, carries between words lost at pc 16642, the last byte of the word lost at pc 12232. Every input file was run against every fault on both releases, comparing whole runs (counter build) and the site word (capture build).
cleared.result: Site-level tests catch every fault: pc 22378 q128 112 and ordinary 5 scenarios differ; pc 22639 q96 80 and ordinary 21; pc 15519 prologue 44 and hook 324; pc 16642 35; pc 12232 756. Whole-run comparisons catch only the pc 12232 fault (588 of 1,348). The other four change no PoolManager result, for reasons the source fixes: a remainder smaller than the true one leaves (prod0 - r) >> k unchanged, so the quotient at FullMath.sol:66-75 is the same; the SAR result at pc 15519 is consumed only by SIGNEXTEND 15 at pc 15522, which ignores bits 128 to 255; pc 16642 is unreachable. This is why cycle 16 saw no effect of its fault at pc 22639, and it means that whole-output differential testing cannot see faults of these kinds at these sites. They are also faults that move no funds.

cleared.check: Whether Monad's native code for the PoolManager is a function of the bytecode alone, on both releases.
cleared.result: Not under v0.16.5. Its block-exit writer collects stack elements in std::unordered_map<StackElem *, int32_t> dep_counts and emits the writes in that map's iteration order (category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp:1433 and :1466 at v0.16.5), which follows heap addresses. One extra early allocation in the compiling process changes 322 to 414 lines of the 48,757-line asm log of the deployed PoolManager. v0.16.7 replaced the map with a vector in stack index order, with the comment that this keeps the emitted code independent of heap addresses (emitter.cpp:1456-1469 and :1502), and its log is identical across the same perturbations. The orders seen are reorderings of independent stores. Four heap layouts of v0.16.5 give 2,000 of 2,000 cycle 15 scenarios equal between engines with identical native digests, and all v0.16.5 runs of this unit used a third and fourth layout. Different v0.16.5 validators can therefore run different machine code for the same contract, but no case where the order changes a result was found.

cleared.check: Whether this unit applies to the other 20 networks.
cleared.result: The five sites are pcs of Monad's x86 code; no other network runs Monad's emitter. The source-level answers (callers of the constant-denominator copies, the bound on a wrong remainder, the casts that reject quotients of 2^127 and above, the unreachable bytes4 branch, the decoder bound before pc 12232) hold for the bytecode on every network, and the opcode battery and scripts recorded in OPCODES.md cover the specified results there.

leads.question: Rerun this unit's site tests (src/run.sh and src/faults.sh in the work directory) and the asm checks on the next Monad release, and check whether a v0.16.5 validator's block-exit write order can ever change a result, for example by building v0.16.5 with an allocator that randomises addresses and replaying the cycle 16 mined transactions.
leads.why: v0.16.5, which cycle 16 read as the release the node documentation lists for mainnet (not refetched here), emits code that depends on heap addresses; only reorderings of independent stores were seen, and a release that changes the emitter again needs the exact-site tests, because whole-output comparisons cannot see faults at four of these five sites.

leadResults.answer: The two mul_mod2 sites were run in the PoolManager's own blocks (entries 0x5703 and 0x5810, arms identical to the deployed build's) with prod1 = 1 and prod0 = 0, 1, 2^96, 2^96 + 1, 2^128 - 1, 2^128 and 2^128 + 1, with the largest allowed prod1 and 256 limb-edge combinations: native = interpreter = Python on v0.16.7 and v0.16.5, 274 and 200 executions, and ordinary swaps reach pc 22639 with prod1 = 1 in 57 scenarios, also equal. Callers: Position.update (Q128, pc 22378) and SqrtPriceMath.getAmount1Delta (Q96, pc 22639). A correct remainder never exceeds prod0 for these denominators, the arm cannot write a value at or above N, and any remainder below N still gives a quotient of at least 2^160 - 1 or 2^128 - 1, which the toInt128 casts of Pool.sol reject, so no amount below 2^127 can be accepted. A planted fault at each site is caught by the site-level tests; whole-run comparisons cannot see a smaller remainder because it leaves the quotient unchanged.

pc 15519 is the sar(128) of BeforeSwapDelta.getSpecifiedDelta on a hook's return word (the source map's BalanceDelta.sol:62-64 is the same assembly text) and runs only for hooks with BEFORE_SWAP_RETURNS_DELTA_FLAG. 654 swap scenarios through a returns-delta hook double and 116 block entries give 764 executions, native = interpreter = Python on both releases; returned deltas include amount0 = -1, -2^127, 2^127 - 1 and 0 with amount1 negative and the mirror cases. pc 16642 is the bytes4 mask for hook calldata shorter than 4 bytes, which no call can produce; it ran 47 times through a block entry with equal results. Marker counts: pc 15519 764, pc 16642 47.
